cor-compression-ui.title: Compressions Are Contractions
cor-compression-ui.html: Let A∈Mn(F) and let P∈Mn(F) be an orthogonal projection. Then |||PAP|||≤|||A||| for every unitarily invariant norm.

cor-eckart-young-ui.title: Eckart–Young Theorem in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm
cor-eckart-young-ui.title_html: Eckart–Young Theorem in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm
cor-eckart-young-ui.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F) with singular values σ1≥⋯≥σp, p=min(m,n), let 0≤k≤p, and let Ak be a truncation of @def-truncated-svd. Then for every B∈Mm×n(F) with rankB≤k and every unitarily invariant norm on Mm×n(F), |||A−Ak||| ≤ |||A−B|||, and the minimum value is |||A−Ak|||=Φ(σk+1,…,σp,0,…,0), where Φ is the symmetric gauge of the norm.

cor-gauge-between-infinity-and-one.title: A Symmetric Gauge Is Trapped Between Two Norms
cor-gauge-between-infinity-and-one.title_html: A Symmetric Gauge Is Trapped Between Two Norms
cor-gauge-between-infinity-and-one.html: Let Φ be a symmetric gauge function on Rn. Then Φ(ej)=Φ(e1) for every j, and Φ(e1)‖x‖∞ ≤ Φ(x) ≤ Φ(e1)‖x‖1(x∈Rn).

cor-harmonic-geometric-arithmetic.title: Harmonic, Geometric and Arithmetic
cor-harmonic-geometric-arithmetic.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F) be positive definite. Then (A−1+B−12)−1 ⪯ A#B ⪯ A+B2.

cor-hoffman-wielandt-again.title: Hoffman–Wielandt for Hermitian Matrices, Again
cor-hoffman-wielandt-again.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F) be Hermitian. Then ∑i=1n(λi(A)−λi(B))2 ≤ ‖A−B‖F2.

cor-log-operator-monotone.title: The Logarithm Is Operator Monotone
cor-log-operator-monotone.html: The function t↦log⁡t is operator monotone on (0,∞).

cor-majorization-convex-hull.title: Majorization Is Membership in a Permutation Polytope
cor-majorization-convex-hull.title_html: Majorization Is Membership in a Permutation Polytope
cor-majorization-convex-hull.html: Let x,y∈Rn. Then x≺y⟺x∈conv{Pσy:σ∈Sn}.

cor-monotone-order-two.title: The Criterion at Order Two
cor-monotone-order-two.html: Let I be an interval with more than one point and let f∈C1(I). Then f is monotone of order 2 on I if and only if f′(t)≥0  for all t∈I,andf[s,t]2≤f′(s)f′(t)  for all s,t∈I.

cor-operator-convex-compression.title: Compression
cor-operator-convex-compression.html: Let I be an interval with 0∈I, let f:I→R be operator convex with f(0)≤0, let A∈Mn(F) be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I, and let P∈Mn(F) be the matrix of an orthogonal projection. Then spec(PAP)⊆I and f(PAP) ⪯ Pf(A)P.

cor-operator-convex-log.title: Two Operator Convex Functions from the Logarithm
cor-operator-convex-log.title_html: Two Operator Convex Functions from the Logarithm
cor-operator-convex-log.html: The functions t↦−log⁡t and t↦tlog⁡t are operator convex on (0,∞).

cor-polar-nearest-ui.title: The Polar Factor Is Nearest in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm
cor-polar-nearest-ui.title_html: The Polar Factor Is Nearest in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm
cor-polar-nearest-ui.html: Let A∈Mn(C) with polar decomposition A=W|A| (@thm-polar-decomposition). Then for every unitary Q∈Mn(C) and every unitarily invariant norm on Mn(C), |||A−W||| ≤ |||A−Q|||.

cor-power-operator-monotone.title: The Operator Monotone Powers
cor-power-operator-monotone.html: Let p∈R. The function t↦tp is operator monotone on (0,∞) if and only if 0≤p≤1. For those p the statement extends to [0,∞): if A⪰B⪰0 are Hermitian of the same size, then Ap⪰Bp.

cor-product-schur-concave.title: The Product Is Schur-Concave
cor-product-schur-concave.html: Let y∈Rn have non-negative entries and let x≺y. Then every entry of x is non-negative, and x1x2⋯xn ≥ y1y2⋯yn.

cor-relative-entropy.title: Non-negativity of the Relative Entropy
cor-relative-entropy.html: Let A,B∈Mn(C) be positive definite with trA=trB=1. Then tr(A(log⁡A−log⁡B)) ≥ 0.

cor-trace-duality.title: Duality of Unitarily Invariant Norms
cor-trace-duality.html: Let |||⋅||| be a unitarily invariant norm on Mm×n(F) (@def-unitarily-invariant-norm) with symmetric gauge Φ on Rp, p=min(m,n), so that |||A|||=Φ(σ(A)) (@lem-ui-norm-of-diagonal). Define |||B|||∗:=max{|tr(B∗A)| : A∈Mm×n(F), |||A|||≤1}. Then |||B|||∗=Φ∗(σ(B)), where Φ∗ is the dual gauge of @def-dual-gauge. In particular |||⋅|||∗ is again a unitarily invariant norm, the trace norm |||⋅|||(p) of @def-ky-fan-norm and the spectral norm ‖⋅‖2 are dual to each other, and the Frobenius norm is self-dual.

def-divided-difference.title: Divided Difference
def-divided-difference.html: Let f:I→R be differentiable. For s,t∈I, the divided difference of f is f[s,t]:={f(s)−f(t)s−t,s≠t,f′(t),s=t.

def-doubly-substochastic.title: Doubly Substochastic Matrix
def-doubly-substochastic.html:
A matrix D=(dkl)∈Mp(R) is doubly substochastic if

  1. dkl≥0 for all k,l;
  2. ∑l=1pdkl≤1 for every row index k; and
  3. ∑k=1pdkl≤1 for every column index l.

def-dual-gauge.title: Dual Gauge
def-dual-gauge.html: Let Φ be a symmetric gauge function on Rn. Its dual gauge is the dual norm of @def-dual-norm, Φ∗(y)=max{⟨x,y⟩:x∈Rn, Φ(x)≤1}.

def-geometric-mean.title: Geometric Mean of Positive Definite Matrices
def-geometric-mean.title_html: Geometric Mean of Positive Definite Matrices
def-geometric-mean.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F) with A≻0 and B≻0. Their geometric mean is A#B := A1/2(A−1/2BA−1/2)1/2A1/2, where A1/2 is the positive square root of @thm-psd-square-root, A−1/2:=(A1/2)−1, and the outer exponent 12 is again the positive square root.

def-ky-fan-gauge.title: Ky Fan Gauge
def-ky-fan-gauge.html: For 1≤k≤n, the k-th Ky Fan gauge on Rn is Φk(x)=∑i=1k|x|i↓, the sum of the k largest absolute values of the entries of x.

def-ky-fan-norm.title: Ky Fan k-Norms
def-ky-fan-norm.html: For 1≤k≤p, the Ky Fan k-norm of A∈Mm×n(F) is |||A|||(k)=∑i=1kσi(A), the sum of the k largest singular values. For k=1 it is the spectral norm ‖A‖2; for k=p it is called the trace norm.

def-loewner-matrix.title: Loewner Matrix
def-loewner-matrix.html: Let f:I→R be differentiable and let t1,…,tn∈I. The Loewner matrix of f at these points is Lf(t1,…,tn):=(f[ti,tj])i,j=1n∈Mn(R).

def-matrix-contraction.title: Contraction
def-matrix-contraction.html: Let V∈Mn×m(F). Then V is a contraction if V∗V⪯Im, that is, if ‖Vx‖≤‖x‖ for every x∈Fm. It is an isometry if V∗V=Im.

def-matrix-integral.title: Integral of a Continuous Matrix-Valued Function
def-matrix-integral.title_html: Integral of a Continuous Matrix-Valued Function
def-matrix-integral.html: Let M:[a,b]→Mp×q(C) be continuous. Its integral ∫abM(s)ds ∈ Mp×q(C) is the matrix J of @prp-riemann-sums-converge. For a continuous M on an open or half-open interval with endpoints a<b, where a=−∞ or b=+∞ is allowed, the improper integral ∫abM(s)ds is the matrix J′, if one exists, such that ∫αkβkM(s)ds ⟶ J′entrywise for every pair of sequences with αk→a, βk→b and a<αk<βk<b. The integral is then said to converge.

def-monotone-of-order-n.title: Monotone of Order n
def-monotone-of-order-n.html: Let n≥1 and let f:I→R. Then f is monotone of order n on I if, for all Hermitian A,B∈Mn(F) whose spectra lie in I, A⪰B⟹f(A)⪰f(B).

def-schur-concave.title: Schur-Concave Function
def-schur-concave.html: With A as in @def-schur-convex, a function G:A→R is Schur-concave if −G is Schur-convex, that is, if x≺y⟹G(x)≥G(y) for all x,y∈A; and strictly Schur-concave if −G is strictly Schur-convex.

def-schur-convex.title: Schur-Convex Function
def-schur-convex.html: Let A⊆Rn be symmetric and convex, and let G:A→R. Then G is Schur-convex if x≺y⟹G(x)≤G(y) for all x,y∈A. It is strictly Schur-convex if the inequality is strict whenever x↓≠y↓.

def-symmetric-gauge.title: Symmetric Gauge Function
def-symmetric-gauge.html:
A symmetric gauge function on Rn is a norm Φ:Rn→R (@def-norm) such that

  1. Φ(Pσx)=Φ(x) for every permutation matrix Pσ and every x∈Rn (permutation invariance);
  2. Φ(ε1x1,…,εnxn)=Φ(x) for all signs εi∈{+1,−1} and every x∈Rn (sign invariance).

def-t-transform.title: T-transform
def-t-transform.html: Let n≥2, let 1≤j<k≤n, and let Q∈Mn(R) be the permutation matrix (@def-permutation-matrix) of the transposition interchanging j and k. For a real number t with 0≤t≤1, the matrix T=(1−t)I+tQ is called a T-transform, and we say that it acts on the pair {j,k}.

def-unitarily-invariant-norm.title: Unitarily Invariant Norm
def-unitarily-invariant-norm.html: A unitarily invariant norm on Mm×n(F) is a norm |||⋅||| on Mm×n(F), regarded as a vector space over F, such that |||UAV|||=|||A||| for every A∈Mm×n(F) and all unitary U∈Mm(F), V∈Mn(F).

eq-dilation-spectrum-positions.html: λi(H(M))={σi(M)1≤i≤p,0p<i≤N−p,−σN+1−i(M)N−p<i≤N.

eq-gauge-depends-on-sorted-moduli.html: Φ(x)=Φ(|x|↓)(x∈Rn),

eq-gauge-of-a-diagonal.html: |||diagm,n(x)|||=Φ(x)(x∈Rp),

eq-lidskii-majorization.html: 𝛌𝛌𝛌λ(A)−λ(B) ≺ λ(A−B).

eq-mirsky-weak-majorization.html: 𝛅|δ| ≺w σ(A−B)in Rp.

eq-singular-values-unitary-invariant.html: σ(UAV)=σ(A).

eq-t-transform-action.html: (Ty)j=(1−t)yj+tyk,(Ty)k=tyj+(1−t)yk,(Ty)i=yi(i≠j,k).

eq-truncation-error-singular-values.html: σi(A−Ak)=σk+i(A)(1≤i≤p),

eq-von-neumann-weights.html: tr(A∗B)=∑k=1p∑l=1pσk(A)σl(B)mklnlk,

exm-cube-not-operator-convex.title: The Cube Is Convex and Not Operator Convex
exm-cube-not-operator-convex.title_html: The Cube Is Convex and Not Operator Convex
exm-cube-not-operator-convex.html: Let A=(1000),B=(2111). Show that A⪰0 and B≻0, and that with θ=12 the inequality required of f(t)=t3 on [0,∞) fails.

exm-dominating-vector.title: Filling from the bottom
exm-dominating-vector.html: Let x=(4,1,1) and y=(5,3,2). Verify x≺wy and produce a z with x≤z and z≺y.

exm-eckart-young-four-norms.title: One matrix, four norms
exm-eckart-young-four-norms.html: Let A=(6−40830001)∈M3(R). Find A1 and A2, and tabulate the approximation errors in the spectral, Frobenius, trace and Ky Fan 2-norms. Compare A1 with the rank-one competitor C=diag(0,0,1).

exm-exp-not-monotone.title: The exponential is not operator monotone
exm-exp-not-monotone.title_html: The exponential is not operator monotone
exm-exp-not-monotone.html: Show that t↦et is not operator monotone on R, and exhibit two 2×2 Hermitian matrices witnessing the failure.

exm-golden-thompson-two-by-two.title: The inequality on a two-by-two family
exm-golden-thompson-two-by-two.title_html: The inequality on a two-by-two family
exm-golden-thompson-two-by-two.html: For real a,b let A=(a00−a),B=(0bb0). Compute both sides of Golden–Thompson, and decide when the inequality is strict.

exm-hlp-four-vector.title: Four coordinates, two transforms
exm-hlp-four-vector.html: Let y=(7,5,3,1) and x=(5,5,4,2). Verify x≺y, run the construction of @thm-hardy-littlewood-polya, and write out the resulting D.

exm-karamata-numbers.title: One majorization, four inequalities
exm-karamata-numbers.html: Let y=(5,3,1,1) and x=(3,3,2,2). Check that x≺y, and write down what @thm-karamata gives for ϕ(t)=t2, for ϕ(t)=|t−2|, and for ϕ(t)=max{t−2,0}.

exm-lidskii-two-by-two.title: A pair to keep in mind
exm-lidskii-two-by-two.title_html: A pair to keep in mind
exm-lidskii-two-by-two.html: Let A=(2222),B=(0−1−10). Compute the three eigenvalue lists and check @eq-lidskii-majorization.

exm-loewner-matrix-sqrt.title: A Cauchy Matrix
exm-loewner-matrix-sqrt.html: Let f(t)=t on (0,∞) and take the points 1,4,9. Compute Lf(1,4,9) and decide whether it is positive semidefinite.

exm-loewner-matrix-square.title: The Loewner Matrix of the Square
exm-loewner-matrix-square.title_html: The Loewner Matrix of the Square
exm-loewner-matrix-square.html: Let f(t)=t2 on [0,∞) and let s≠t be points of [0,∞). Compute Lf(s,t) and decide whether it is positive semidefinite.

exm-logdet-convex.title: The logarithm of the determinant
exm-logdet-convex.html: Let f(t)=−log⁡t on I=(0,∞), so that the matrices in play are the positive definite Hermitian ones. Identify trf(A), and check the resulting inequality for A=(1004),B=(2112),θ=12.

exm-schatten-norms.title: The Schatten norms
exm-schatten-norms.html: The letter p is reserved in this section for min(m,n), so write the exponent as r. For 1≤r≤∞, the Schatten r-norm is |||A|||Sr=‖σ(A)‖r=(∑i=1pσi(A)r)1/r, read as |||A|||S∞=σ1(A) at r=∞. Identify S1, S2 and S∞, and explain why each |||⋅|||Sr is a unitarily invariant norm.

exm-schur-convex-first.title: Four functions on \nR^n
exm-schur-convex-first.title_html: Four functions on Rn
exm-schur-convex-first.html:
Decide which of the following are Schur-convex, and which are Schur-concave, on A=Rn.

  1. G(x)=∑ixi2.
  2. G(x)=maxixi.
  3. G(x)=∑ixi.
  4. G(x)=∑ixi3, for n=3.

exm-sum-not-majorization.title: Weak majorization is the most that holds
exm-sum-not-majorization.title_html: Weak majorization is the most that holds
exm-sum-not-majorization.html: Let A=diag(1,0) and B=diag(−1,0). Then σ(A)=σ(B)=(1,0), so σ(A)+σ(B)=(2,0), while A+B=0 has σ(A+B)=(0,0). The totals are 0 and 2, so σ(A+B)≺σ(A)+σ(B) is false, although the weak majorization holds with room to spare.

exm-symmetric-gauge-examples.title: The p-norms, the Ky Fan gauges, and size one
exm-symmetric-gauge-examples.title_html: The p-norms, the Ky Fan gauges, and size one
exm-symmetric-gauge-examples.html:
Check each against @def-symmetric-gauge.

  1. ‖⋅‖p for 1≤p≤∞.
  2. For 1≤k≤n, the function Φk(x)=∑i≤k|x|i↓, the sum of the k largest absolute values.
  3. On R1, the function Φ(x)=c|x| for a constant c>0.

exm-t-transform-basic.title: Three T-transforms, and two impostors
exm-t-transform-basic.html:
Take n=3 and y=(6,3,0).

  1. Compute Ty for the T-transform on {1,3} with t=13, and for the ones with t=0 and t=1.
  2. Is the matrix 12(I+P), with P the permutation matrix of the 3-cycle 1↦2↦3↦1, a T-transform?
  3. Is −I+2Q, with Q the transposition matrix of {1,2}, a T-transform?

exm-three-matrices-fails.title: The three-matrix version fails
exm-three-matrices-fails.html: Let t>0 and let P1,P2,P3 be the orthogonal projections of R2 onto the three lines through the origin at angles 0, 2π/3 and 4π/3: P1=(1000),P2=14(1−3−33),P3=14(1333). Put A=tP1, B=tP2, C=tP3, all symmetric. Compute both sides of the three-matrix inequality and show that it fails.

exm-ui-norm-examples.title: The two familiar norms
exm-ui-norm-examples.html:
Check each against @def-unitarily-invariant-norm.

  1. The Frobenius norm ‖A‖F.
  2. The spectral norm ‖A‖2.

exm-von-neumann-two-by-two.title: A strict case and an equality case
exm-von-neumann-two-by-two.title_html: A strict case and an equality case
exm-von-neumann-two-by-two.html: Let A=(2001),B=(12−12169),B′=(200015). Check that B and B′ have the same singular values, and compare the two sides of @thm-von-neumann-trace for the pairs (A,B) and (A,B′).

exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-a1.title: A1
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-a1.html:
1. State Karamata’s inequality, with all its hypotheses.
  2. Which test functions prove @prp-majorization-from-convex, and which clause of @def-majorization does each one give?
  3. Define Schur-convex and Schur-concave.
  4. True or false: every Schur-convex function on Rn is convex. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: every convex function on Rn is Schur-convex. Justify your answer.
  6. State what @thm-trace-convex says for f(t)=t2, and identify the resulting function of A.

exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-b1.title: B1: Four consequences of one majorization
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-b1.title_html: B1: Four consequences of one majorization
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-b1.html:
Let y=(6,2,1,1) and x=(4,3,2,1).

  1. Verify that x≺y.
  2. Compute ∑ixi2 and ∑iyi2, and ∑imax{xi−3,0} and ∑imax{yi−3,0}. Name the theorem each comparison illustrates.
  3. Compute ∏ixi and ∏iyi. Hence check @cor-product-schur-concave.
  4. Give a convex ϕ:R→R for which the two sides are equal.

exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-b2.title: B2: Which are Schur-convex?
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-b2.html:
Determine which of the following functions are Schur-convex on the stated symmetric convex set. Justify your answer, naming the theorem used or giving a counterexample.

  1. G(x)=maxixi−minixi on Rn.
  2. G(x)=∑i|xi| on Rn.
  3. G(x)=x1+2x2 on R2.
  4. G(x)=∑ixi on A={x∈Rn:xi>0 for every i}.

exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-b3.title: B3: Trace convexity on two-by-two matrices
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-b3.title_html: B3: Trace convexity on two-by-two matrices
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-b3.html:
1. Let f(t)=t2, A=diag(2,0), B=(1111) and θ=12. Compute trf(A), trf(B) and trf(C) for C=12(A+B), and verify @thm-trace-convex.
  2. Let f(t)=−log⁡t, A=I2, B=diag(4,14) and θ=12. Do the same, and state the inequality in terms of determinants.

exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-c1.title: C1: Entropy
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-c1.html:
For x in A={x∈Rn:xi>0 for every i}, let H(x)=−∑ixilog⁡xi.

  1. Prove that g(t)=tlog⁡t is convex on (0,∞). Hint: apply @thm-jensen to the concave log, with the points 1/a, 1/b and cleverly chosen weights.
  2. Deduce that H is Schur-concave on A.
  3. Deduce that H(x)≤log⁡n for every x∈A with ∑ixi=1, with equality when x=(1n,…,1n).

exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-c2.title: C2: Three norms under majorization
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-c2.html: Let x≺y in Rn. Prove that ‖x‖1≤‖y‖1,‖x‖2≤‖y‖2,‖x‖∞≤‖y‖∞. Which of the three needs @thm-karamata, and which follows from @def-majorization alone?

exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-c3.title: C3: One convex function is not enough
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-c3.title_html: C3: One convex function is not enough
exr-convex-functions-and-majorization-c3.html:
Let x=(2,−1,−1) and y=(1,1,−2).

  1. Show that ∑ixi=∑iyi and ∑ixi2=∑iyi2, yet neither x≺y nor y≺x.
  2. Exhibit a convex ϕ with ∑iϕ(xi)>∑iϕ(yi), and another with the inequality reversed. Explain how this is consistent with @prp-majorization-from-convex.

exr-golden-thompson-a1.title: A1
exr-golden-thompson-a1.html:
1. State the Golden–Thompson inequality, with its hypotheses.
  2. State Lie’s product formula, and say for which matrices it holds.
  3. True or false: for Hermitian A,B the matrix eAeB is positive semidefinite. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: treA+B≤tr(eBeA) for Hermitian A,B. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: treA+B+C≤tr(eAeBeC) for Hermitian A,B,C. Justify your answer.
  6. Where in the proof of @thm-golden-thompson is the hypothesis that A and B are Hermitian used?

exr-golden-thompson-b1.title: B1: Both sides, exactly
exr-golden-thompson-b1.html:
Let A=(000−2),B=(0110).

  1. Compute eA, eB and tr(eAeB) exactly.
  2. Compute treA+B exactly, and verify @thm-golden-thompson numerically to three decimal places.

exr-golden-thompson-b2.title: B2: The trace power inequality on integers
exr-golden-thompson-b2.title_html: B2: The trace power inequality on integers
exr-golden-thompson-b2.html:
Let X=diag(2,1) and Y=(1111).

  1. Check that X and Y are positive semidefinite, and compute tr((XY)m) and tr(XmYm) for m=1,2,4.
  2. Verify @lem-trace-power-inequality (b) in these three cases, and say for which of them it is strict.

exr-golden-thompson-b3.title: B3: Klein with the exponential
exr-golden-thompson-b3.html: Let A,B∈Mn(C) be Hermitian. Use @thm-klein with f(t)=et to prove treA ≥ treB+tr((A−B)eB), and check the inequality for A=diag(1,0), B=0.

exr-golden-thompson-c1.title: C1: Two out of three is enough
exr-golden-thompson-c1.title_html: C1: Two out of three is enough
exr-golden-thompson-c1.html:
Let A,B,C∈Mn(C) be Hermitian. Prove that treA+B+C ≤ tr(eAeBeC) holds whenever some two of the three matrices commute, treating the three cases separately. Explain why this does not contradict @exm-three-matrices-fails.

Hint: @thm-exponential-properties (d), and the cyclic invariance of the trace.

exr-golden-thompson-c2.title: C2: The symmetric Lie formula
exr-golden-thompson-c2.html:
Let A,B∈Mn(C).

  1. Prove that eA+B=limk→∞(eA/2keB/keA/2k)k.
  2. Deduce that for Hermitian A,B one also has treA+B≤tr(eA/2eBeA/2), and explain why this is not a new inequality.

Hint: for (a), rerun Steps 2–4 of the proof of @lem-lie-product with the new Tk; only the constant M changes.

exr-golden-thompson-c3.title: C3: When is the relative entropy zero?
exr-golden-thompson-c3.title_html: C3: When is the relative entropy zero?
exr-golden-thompson-c3.html:
Let A,B∈Mn(C) be positive definite with trA=trB=1.

  1. Show that equality holds in @lem-convex-gradient-inequality for f(t)=tlog⁡t only when s=t.
  2. Deduce that tr(A(log⁡A−log⁡B))=0 forces A=B.

Hint: for (b), look at which coefficients cij in the proof of @thm-klein can be non-zero.

exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-a1.title: A1
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-a1.html:
1. Define a T-transform, and say which coordinates of a vector it can change.
  2. State the Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya theorem in full.
  3. True or false: if x=Sy with S row-stochastic (non-negative entries, every row adding up to 1), then x≺y. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: if x≺y, the doubly stochastic D with x=Dy is unique. Justify your answer.
  5. In @lem-t-transform-step, why is j chosen as the largest index with yj>xj rather than the smallest?
  6. Why can the number of coordinates in which two decreasing vectors x≺y agree never be exactly n−1?

exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-b1.title: B1: Run the construction
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-b1.html: Let y=(9,5,4) and x=(6,6,6). Verify x≺y, produce T-transforms T1,T2 with x=T2T1y by the recipe of @lem-t-transform-step, and write out D=T2T1. Hence check that D is doubly stochastic.

exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-b2.title: B2: Determine which are majorizations
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-b2.html:
For each pair, determine whether x≺y. Where it holds, exhibit a doubly stochastic D with x=Dy; where it fails, name the clause of @def-majorization and the value of k at which it fails. Justify your answer.

  1. x=(2,2,2), y=(4,1,1).
  2. x=(3,1,0), y=(2,2,0).
  3. x=(1,3,0), y=(2,0,2).
  4. x=(1,1), y=(2,1).

exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-b3.title: B3: Into the polytope
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-b3.html: Let y=(4,2,0) and x=(2,2,2). Using @cor-majorization-convex-hull, write x explicitly as a convex combination of rearrangements of y, in two different ways.

exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-c1.title: C1: Row-stochastic is not enough, twice over
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-c1.title_html: C1: Row-stochastic is not enough, twice over
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-c1.html:
Let S∈Mn(R) be row-stochastic: every entry is non-negative and every row adds up to 1.

  1. Give such an S and a y∈R2 with Sy⊀y.
  2. Prove that if Sy≺y for every y∈Rn, then S is doubly stochastic.

Hint for (b): test the hypothesis on the standard basis vectors.

exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-c2.title: C2: Transitivity, a second time
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-c2.html:
1. Prove that if A,B∈Ωn then AB∈Ωn.
  2. Hence deduce that x≺y and y≺z imply x≺z, and compare this route with the proof of @prp-majorization-basic (b).

exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-c3.title: C3: The count n - 1 cannot be improved
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-c3.title_html: C3: The count n−1 cannot be improved
exr-hardy-littlewood-polya-c3.html:
Let n≥2, y=(n,0,…,0) and x=(1,1,…,1) in Rn. For z∈Rn, write supp(z)={i:zi≠0}.

  1. Show that x≺y.
  2. Let T be a T-transform. Prove that |supp(Tz)|≤|supp(z)|+1 for every z∈Rn.
  3. Deduce that no product of fewer than n−1 T-transforms sends y to x.

exr-ky-fan-dominance-a1.title: A1
exr-ky-fan-dominance-a1.html:
1. State @thm-ky-fan-dominance, and say which family of norms proves the direction that is not a direct consequence of Sections 3 and 4.
  2. Define the Ky Fan k-norm and say why it is a unitarily invariant norm.
  3. Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: if ‖A‖F≤‖B‖F and ‖A‖2≤‖B‖2, then |||A|||≤|||B||| for every unitarily invariant norm.
  4. In the proof of @cor-eckart-young-ui, where is the hypothesis rankB≤k used?
  5. Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: for A∈Mn(C) invertible, the nearest unitary matrix in the trace norm is the same as the nearest one in the Frobenius norm.

exr-ky-fan-dominance-b1.title: B1: Dominance by hand
exr-ky-fan-dominance-b1.html:
Let A,B∈M3(R) have singular values σ(A)=(3,2,2) and σ(B)=(4,3,1).

  1. Determine whether |||A|||≤|||B||| for every unitarily invariant norm.
  2. Answer the same question for σ(A′)=(3,3,2) in place of σ(A).

exr-ky-fan-dominance-b2.title: B2: Best approximations of a 2 by 2 matrix
exr-ky-fan-dominance-b2.title_html: B2: Best approximations of a 2 by 2 matrix
exr-ky-fan-dominance-b2.html: Let A=(344−3). Compute σ(A), find the best rank-one approximation, and compute the error in the spectral, Frobenius and trace norms. What is unusual about this matrix?

exr-ky-fan-dominance-b3.title: B3: A compression
exr-ky-fan-dominance-b3.html: Let A=(2113) and let P=e1e1⊤. Compute |||PAP||| and |||A||| for the trace norm, and check @cor-compression-ui.

exr-ky-fan-dominance-c1.title: C1: Dominance for sums
exr-ky-fan-dominance-c1.html:
Let A,B∈Mm×n(C).

  1. Prove that |||A+B|||≤|||A|||+|||B||| follows from @lem-singular-value-subadditive together with @thm-gauge-monotone-under-majorization (b), without using that |||⋅||| is a norm.
  2. Deduce that ∑i≤kσi(A+B)≤∑i≤kσi(A)+∑i≤kσi(B) for every k.

exr-ky-fan-dominance-c2.title: C2: Distance to the singular matrices, in every norm
exr-ky-fan-dominance-c2.title_html: C2: Distance to the singular matrices, in every norm
exr-ky-fan-dominance-c2.html:
Let A∈Mn(C) be invertible with singular values σ1≥⋯≥σn>0, and let |||⋅||| be a unitarily invariant norm with gauge Φ.

  1. Prove that min{|||A−B|||:B∈Mn(C) singular}=Φ(σn,0,…,0).
  2. Deduce that this minimum equals σnΦ(e1), and identify it for the spectral, Frobenius and trace norms.

Hint: a matrix is singular exactly when its rank is at most n−1.

exr-ky-fan-dominance-c3.title: C3: Unitary matrices are far apart
exr-ky-fan-dominance-c3.title_html: C3: Unitary matrices are far apart
exr-ky-fan-dominance-c3.html:
Let U,Q∈Mn(C) be unitary with U≠Q.

  1. Prove that σ(U−Q)=(|μ1−1|,…,|μn−1|)↓, where μ1,…,μn are the eigenvalues of Q∗U.
  2. Deduce that |||U−Q|||=|||diag(μ1−1,…,μn−1)||| for every unitarily invariant norm, and that the trace-norm distance between two distinct unitary matrices can be as large as 2n.

exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-a1.title: A1
exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-a1.html:
1. State the majorization @eq-lidskii-majorization, and say which chapter proves it.
  2. State @thm-lidskii-ui, and say what 𝛌𝛌diag(λ(A)−λ(B)) means.
  3. Determine whether the following is true for Hermitian A,B, and justify your answer: ∑i|λi(A)−λi(B)|≤∑i|λi(A−B)|.
  4. Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: @thm-mirsky-ui holds with the singular values of A and B listed in increasing order on the left.
  5. Where in the proof of @thm-mirsky-ui is it used that A and B have the same size?

exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-b1.title: B1: Running the three consequences
exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-b1.html:
Let A=diag(5,1,0) and let B=A−E with E=(002000200).

  1. Compute 𝛌λ(B) and 𝛌λ(E).
  2. Verify @eq-lidskii-majorization for this pair.
  3. Verify @thm-lidskii-ui in the spectral, Frobenius and trace norms, and @cor-hoffman-wielandt-again.

exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-b2.title: B2: Singular values of a one-entry change
exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-b2.title_html: B2: Singular values of a one-entry change
exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-b2.html: Let A=(3113) and B=(3103). Compute both sides of @thm-mirsky-ui in the trace norm, and compare with what @cor-singular-value-perturbation gives on its own.

exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-b3.title: B3: A bound with no norm in sight
exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-b3.title_html: B3: A bound with no norm in sight
exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-b3.html: Let A,B∈Mn(C) be Hermitian with ‖A−B‖2≤ε. Prove that ∑i|λi(A)−λi(B)|≤nε, and give a pair for which this is an equality.

exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-c1.title: C1: The Schatten norms
exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-c1.html:
Recall the Schatten r-norm |||M|||Sr=(∑iσi(M)r)1/r of @exm-schatten-norms, the unitarily invariant norm with gauge ‖⋅‖r, and let 1≤r<∞.

  1. Prove that for Hermitian A,B∈Mn(C), ∑i|λi(A)−λi(B)|r≤∑i|λi(A−B)|r, in two ways: from @thm-lidskii-convex and from @thm-lidskii-ui.
  2. Deduce the same statement for singular values, with σ in place of λ and A,B arbitrary of the same size.

exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-c2.title: C2: What the dilation costs
exr-lidskii-and-its-consequences-c2.html:
Let A,B∈Mm×n(C) and let H(⋅) be the Hermitian dilation.

  1. Prove that |||H(A)||| and |||A||| cannot be compared in general, by computing both for the Frobenius norm and for the spectral norm with A=I2.
  2. Explain, in one or two sentences, why the proof of @thm-mirsky-ui is nevertheless free of any such factor.
  3. Deduce @cor-eckart-young-ui from @thm-mirsky-ui, and say why Section 6 nevertheless proved it another way.

Hint: for (c), a matrix of rank at most k has σi=0 for i>k.

exr-loewner-matrices-a1.title: A1
exr-loewner-matrices-a1.html:
1. Define f[s,t] for s=t, and say what hypothesis on f the definition needs.
  2. Write down Lf(t1,t2,t3) in terms of divided differences, and say why it is Hermitian.
  3. State @thm-loewner-matrix-criterion, and say which of its two directions uses the Schur product theorem.
  4. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if Lf(t1,t2)⪰0 for all t1,t2∈I, then f is operator monotone on I.
  5. What does @thm-derivative-of-a-matrix-function give when H is diagonal?

exr-loewner-matrices-b1.title: B1: Loewner matrices by hand
exr-loewner-matrices-b1.html:
Compute Lf(1,2) for each of the following, and determine whether it is positive semidefinite. Justify your answer.

  1. f(t)=4+3t on R.
  2. f(t)=t2 on (0,∞).
  3. f(t)=−1/t on (0,∞).
  4. f(t)=t on (0,∞), at the points 1 and 4 instead.

exr-loewner-matrices-b2.title: B2: A derivative, two ways
exr-loewner-matrices-b2.html:
Let A=diag(1,4), let H=(1223) and let f(t)=t2 on (0,∞).

  1. Compute Lf(1,4)∘H.
  2. Expand (A+sH)2 and differentiate at s=0 directly. Check that the two answers agree.

exr-loewner-matrices-b3.title: B3: Refuting order two
exr-loewner-matrices-b3.html:
For each function, use @cor-monotone-order-two to decide whether it is monotone of order 2 on the interval given. Justify your answer.

  1. f(t)=t/(t+1) on (0,∞).
  2. f(t)=t2−6t on (0,1).
  3. f(t)=2t−1/t on (0,∞).
  4. f(t)=t+t2 on (0,∞).

exr-loewner-matrices-c1.title: C1: Powers, directly
exr-loewner-matrices-c1.html:
Let k≥1, let A=diag(t1,…,tn) and let H∈Mn(F) be Hermitian.

  1. Expand (A+sH)k and show that the coefficient of s is ∑p+q=k−1ApHAq, the sum being over integers p,q≥0.
  2. Compute the (i,j) entry of that matrix and identify it with f[ti,tj]hij for f(t)=tk.
  3. Hence prove @thm-derivative-of-a-matrix-function (a) for every polynomial f, without using @lem-functional-calculus-continuous.

exr-loewner-matrices-c2.title: C2: The logarithm at order two
exr-loewner-matrices-c2.title_html: C2: The logarithm at order two
exr-loewner-matrices-c2.html:
1. Prove that r−1/r−2log⁡r≥0 for every r≥1.
  2. Deduce that log is monotone of order 2 on (0,∞).
  3. Deduce that f(t)=−log⁡(1−t) is monotone of order 2 on (0,1), and verify that f is convex there.

Hint for (a): differentiate, and recognize a square.

exr-loewner-matrices-c3.title: C3: Orders are nested
exr-loewner-matrices-c3.html:
Let 1≤m≤n and let f:I→R; in (b) and (c) assume in addition that f∈C1(I), so that the Loewner matrices are defined and @thm-loewner-matrix-criterion applies.

  1. Prove that if f is monotone of order n on I, then it is monotone of order m on I.
  2. Give the corresponding statement about Loewner matrices, and prove it directly from @def-loewner-matrix, without using @thm-loewner-matrix-criterion.
  3. Explain why (a) and (b) together mean that a single failing pair of points rules out operator monotonicity at every order n≥2.

Hint for (a): pad with a scalar block.

exr-loewners-theorem-a1.title: A1
exr-loewners-theorem-a1.html:
1. State what @thm-pick-nevanlinna gives, and say which implication of @thm-loewner rests on it.
  2. Explain in one sentence why an integral of positive semidefinite matrices is positive semidefinite, naming the two properties of the positive semidefinite matrices that the argument uses.
  3. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: “a function that extends to an entire function of z and is increasing on (0,∞) is operator monotone there”.
  4. For which real p is t↦tp operator monotone on (0,∞)? Name the result and say which of its cases needed (A7).
  5. Where in the proof of @thm-loewner is the hypothesis β≥0 used, and what would go wrong without it?

exr-loewners-theorem-b1.title: B1: One matrix integral
exr-loewners-theorem-b1.html: Let M(t)=(2+t112−t),t∈[−1,1]. Show that M(t)⪰0 for every t∈[−1,1], compute ∫−11M(t)dt, and confirm the conclusion of @lem-integral-preserves-loewner for it.

exr-loewners-theorem-b2.title: B2: The constant for the square root
exr-loewners-theorem-b2.title_html: B2: The constant for the square root
exr-loewners-theorem-b2.html:
1. Show that K1/2=∫0∞u−1/2(1+u)−1du=π. Hint: substitute u=w2.
  2. Let A=(5445). Using @lem-power-integral with p=12, evaluate 1π∫0∞s−1/2A(A+sI)−1ds and check the answer against the positive square root of A.

exr-loewners-theorem-b3.title: B3: Which are operator monotone?
exr-loewners-theorem-b3.html:
Determine which of the following are operator monotone on (0,∞). Justify your answer.

  1. f(t)=t2/3.
  2. f(t)=t4/3.
  3. f(t)=3+2log⁡t.
  4. f(t)=−t−1/3.
  5. f(t)=log⁡(1+t).
  6. f(t)=et.

exr-loewners-theorem-c1.title: C1: When the integral loses information
exr-loewners-theorem-c1.title_html: C1: When the integral loses information
exr-loewners-theorem-c1.html:
1. Give a continuous M:[0,1]→M2(R) with every M(t) symmetric, ∫01M⪰0, and M(t)⪰̸0 for some t. Hence the converse of @lem-integral-preserves-loewner fails.
  2. Prove that if M:[a,b]→Mn(C) is continuous with M(t)⪰0 for every t and ∫abM=0, then M(t)=0 for every t.

Hint for (b): a continuous non-negative scalar function with zero integral is zero.

exr-loewners-theorem-c2.title: C2: The cube, by a Loewner matrix
exr-loewners-theorem-c2.title_html: C2: The cube, by a Loewner matrix
exr-loewners-theorem-c2.html:
1. Write down the Loewner matrix Lf(t1,t2) for f(t)=t3 and general t1≠t2, and evaluate its determinant at t1=1, t2=2. What does @thm-loewner-matrix-criterion conclude?
  2. Do the same for f(t)=t1/2 at t1=1, t2=4, and say which result of this section the sign of the determinant illustrates.

exr-loewners-theorem-c3.title: C3: Half of the representation, by hand
exr-loewners-theorem-c3.title_html: C3: Half of the representation, by hand
exr-loewners-theorem-c3.html:
Let 0<p<1, let A⪰B≻0 be Hermitian in Mn(F), and let 0<δ<R. Put Z(δ,R)=∫δRsp−1(A(A+sI)−1−B(B+sI)−1)ds.

  1. Prove that Z(δ,R)⪰0 for every such δ,R, without any statement about improper integrals.
  2. Deduce Ap⪰Bp from (a) and the convergence statement of @lem-power-integral.
  3. Explain why the same argument does not show A2⪰B2, by pointing at the step that fails.

exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-a1.title: A1
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-a1.html:
1. Define A#B for positive definite A,B, and say why each square root in the formula exists.
  2. State the extremal characterization of A#B, and explain in one sentence how it makes the symmetry A#B=B#A obvious.
  3. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: “A1/2B1/2 is positive definite whenever A and B are”.
  4. State the matrix Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality for singular values, @thm-matrix-am-gm — not the one for the geometric mean A#B — and say which one implies the other and how.
  5. Which of A∗A+B∗B and AA∗+BB∗ bounds 2|||A∗B|||, and what goes wrong with the other?

exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-b1.title: B1: A geometric mean, exactly
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-b1.html:
Let A=(5445),B=(13202037).

  1. Verify that A1/2=(2112) and compute C=A−1/2BA−1/2 and A#B.
  2. Check the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality A#B⪯12(A+B) directly, by computing the difference and its eigenvalues.
  3. Verify the extremal characterization for your answer by computing the Schur complement B−XA−1X with X=A#B.

exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-b2.title: B2: The two inequalities on one pair
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-b2.title_html: B2: The two inequalities on one pair
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-b2.html:
Let A=(1101) and B=(1011) in M2(R).

  1. Compute A∗B and AA∗+BB∗, and verify 2σj(A∗B)≤λj(AA∗+BB∗) for j=1,2 using traces and determinants.
  2. Verify @thm-matrix-cauchy-schwarz for this pair in the Frobenius norm.

exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-b3.title: B3: Means of commuting matrices
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-b3.html: Let A=diag(a1,…,an) and B=diag(b1,…,bn) with all ai,bi>0. Compute the three means of @cor-harmonic-geometric-arithmetic and deduce the classical chain of inequalities between the harmonic, geometric and arithmetic means of two positive numbers.

exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c1.title: C1: The determinant of a geometric mean
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c1.title_html: C1: The determinant of a geometric mean
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c1.html:
Let A,B∈Mn(F) be positive definite.

  1. Prove that det(A#B)=detAdetB.
  2. Deduce from @cor-harmonic-geometric-arithmetic that detAdetB≤det(12(A+B)).

Hint for (b): the Loewner order compares determinants of positive definite matrices.

exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c2.title: C2: The geometric mean solves an equation
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c2.title_html: C2: The geometric mean solves an equation
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c2.html:
Let A,B∈Mn(F) be positive definite.

  1. Prove that X=A#B is the only positive definite solution of XA−1X=B.
  2. Use (a) to give a second proof that A#B=B#A.

exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c3.title: C3: Cauchy–Schwarz for the Ky Fan norms, directly
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c3.title_html: C3: Cauchy–Schwarz for the Ky Fan norms, directly
exr-matrix-means-and-inequalities-c3.html:
Let A,B∈Mn(F) and 1≤k≤n.

  1. Let A∗B=WΣZ∗ be a singular value decomposition (@thm-svd), and let Uk and Vk be the matrices of the first k columns of W and of Z. Show that tr(Uk∗A∗BVk)=∑j≤kσj(A∗B).
  2. Deduce, using the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for the Frobenius inner product (@thm-cauchy-schwarz) and the Ky Fan maximum principle (@thm-ky-fan), that ∑j≤kσj(A∗B)≤(∑j≤kλj(A∗A))1/2(∑j≤kλj(B∗B))1/2.

exr-operator-convexity-a1.title: A1
exr-operator-convexity-a1.html:
1. State what it means for f:I→R to be operator convex, and say what the clause “for every n” ranges over.
  2. Explain why an operator convex function is convex, and name a convex function that is not operator convex.
  3. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if f is operator convex on I and c<0, then cf is operator convex on I.
  4. State the Hansen–Pedersen–Jensen inequality, and say which hypothesis fails for f(t)=t2+1.
  5. Is t↦−1/t operator convex on (0,∞)? Is it operator concave there?

exr-operator-convexity-b1.title: B1: Which are operator convex?
exr-operator-convexity-b1.html:
Determine which of the following functions are operator convex on the interval given. Justify your answer.

  1. f(t)=7−3t on R.
  2. f(t)=2t2+5t−1 on R.
  3. f(t)=4t+3 on (0,∞).
  4. f(t)=tt+3 on (0,∞).
  5. f(t)=t3 on [0,∞).

exr-operator-convexity-b2.title: B2: A dilation by hand
exr-operator-convexity-b2.html:
Let V=(12000).

  1. Verify that V is a contraction and compute D1=(I2−V∗V)1/2 and D2=(I2−VV∗)1/2.
  2. Write down the 4×4 matrix U of @lem-block-dilation and verify directly that its first column is a unit vector orthogonal to its third column.

exr-operator-convexity-b3.title: B3: Compression of a square
exr-operator-convexity-b3.html: Let A=(2111),P=(1000). Compute (PAP)2 and PA2P, and verify the inequality of @cor-operator-convex-compression for f(t)=t2. Hence state what the inequality says about the entry in position (1,1).

exr-operator-convexity-c1.title: C1: The square, without the dilation
exr-operator-convexity-c1.title_html: C1: The square, without the dilation
exr-operator-convexity-c1.html:
Let A∈Mn(F) be Hermitian and let V∈Mn×m(F) be a contraction.

  1. Prove that (V∗AV)2⪯V∗A2V directly, without using @thm-jensen-operator.
  2. Which hypothesis of @thm-jensen-operator does your proof use, and which does it not?

Hint for (a): insert I−VV∗.

exr-operator-convexity-c2.title: C2: Shrinking the matrix
exr-operator-convexity-c2.html:
Let I be an interval with 0∈I, let f be operator convex on I with f(0)≤0, and let A∈Mn(F) be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I.

  1. Prove that f(θA)⪯θf(A) for every θ∈[0,1], assuming spec(θA)⊆I.
  2. Give an operator convex f with f(0)>0 for which (a) fails, and say at which θ.
  3. Let V∈Mn×1(F) be a unit column vector and g(t)=t2+1 on R. Write out what @thm-jensen-operator (b) says here, and verify it for A=(2111) and V=e1.

Hint for (a): a scalar multiple of the identity is a contraction when the scalar is small.

exr-operator-convexity-c3.title: C3: What the trace does not see
exr-operator-convexity-c3.title_html: C3: What the trace does not see
exr-operator-convexity-c3.html:
Let A=diag(1,0) and B=(2111) be the matrices of @exm-cube-not-operator-convex, and let f(t)=t3 on [0,∞).

  1. Compute tr(12(A3+B3))−tr((12(A+B))3), and say which theorem makes its sign predictable.
  2. The same defect matrix is indefinite. Explain, in one sentence, why (a) and that fact are consistent.
  3. Give a convex function g on [0,∞) for which the defect matrix at this pair A,B is positive semidefinite, and name the reason.

exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-a1.title: A1
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-a1.html:
1. State @def-symmetric-gauge, naming both invariance clauses and the space the function is defined on.
  2. Explain why Φ(x)=Φ(|x|↓) for every symmetric gauge and every x.
  3. True or false, with a reason: if x≺wy in Rn, then ‖x‖2≤‖y‖2.
  4. Name the hypothesis in @thm-gauge-monotone-under-majorization (b) that part (a) does without, and say where it is used in the proof.

exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-b1.title: B1: Which of these are symmetric gauges
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-b1.title_html: B1: Which of these are symmetric gauges
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-b1.html:
Determine which of the following are symmetric gauge functions on R3. Justify your answer, naming the exact clause that fails when one does.

  1. Φ(x)=|x1|+|x2|+|x3|.
  2. Φ(x)=|x|1↓+|x|2↓.
  3. Φ(x)=(|x1|1/2+|x2|1/2+|x3|1/2)2.
  4. Φ(x)=max(|x1|,|x2|)+|x3|.
  5. Φ(x)=|x1+x2+x3|+|x1−x2|+|x2−x3|.

exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-b2.title: B2: Filling from the bottom
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-b2.html:
Let x=(6,2,2,0) and y=(7,4,3,2) in R4.

  1. Verify that x≺wy and that x⊀y.
  2. Carry out the construction in the proof of @lem-weak-majorization-dominated to produce z with x≤z and z≺y.
  3. Hence bound ‖x‖2 by ‖y‖2 without computing either, and then check the bound numerically.

exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-b3.title: B3: Monotonicity used twice
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-b3.html:
Let Φ be a symmetric gauge function on R3 with Φ(e1)=1.

  1. Prove that 1≤Φ(1,1,0)≤2.
  2. Prove that Φ(2,1,1)≤Φ(3,1,0).
  3. Give a symmetric gauge for which the inequality in (b) is strict, and one for which it is an equality.

exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c1.title: C1: Symmetric gauges detect weak majorization
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c1.title_html: C1: Symmetric gauges detect weak majorization
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c1.html:
Let x,y∈Rn have non-negative entries.

  1. Prove that x≺wy if and only if Φ(x)≤Φ(y) for every symmetric gauge function Φ on Rn.
  2. Prove that x≺y if and only if x≺wy and ∑ixi=∑iyi.
  3. Deduce that x≺y if and only if Φ(x)≤Φ(y) for every symmetric gauge and ∑ixi=∑iyi.

Hint for (a): only finitely many gauges are needed.

exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c2.title: C2: The dual of a Ky Fan gauge
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c2.title_html: C2: The dual of a Ky Fan gauge
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c2.html:
Fix 1≤k≤n and let Φk be the Ky Fan gauge of @def-ky-fan-gauge.

  1. Prove that Φk∗(y)≥max(‖y‖∞, 1k‖y‖1) by exhibiting two competitors.
  2. Let Φk(x)≤1 and let y have non-negative, decreasing entries. Put t=|x|k↓ and split each |xi| as (|xi|−t)++min(|xi|,t). Prove that ∑i(|xi|−t)+≤1−kt and that 0≤t≤1/k.
  3. Deduce Φk∗(y)=max(‖y‖∞,1k‖y‖1), and check the cases k=1 and k=n against @prp-dual-of-one-two-infinity.

exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c3.title: C3: Where each hypothesis is used
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c3.title_html: C3: Where each hypothesis is used
exr-symmetric-gauge-functions-c3.html:
1. Determine whether there is a norm on R2 that is permutation invariant and satisfies Φ(x)≤Φ(y) whenever |xi|≤|yi| for all i, but is not a symmetric gauge function. Justify your answer.
  2. @thm-gauge-monotone-under-majorization (b) needs non-negative entries, while @lem-weak-majorization-dominated does not. Locate the exact step of the proof of the theorem that uses the hypothesis, and explain why x=(0,−10)≺w(0,0)=y breaks it even though the lemma supplies a perfectly good z.
  3. Let x≺wy with x=x↓, and let z be the vector built in the proof of @lem-weak-majorization-dominated. Prove that z≺z′ for every z′ with x≤z′ and ∑izi′=∑iyi, and deduce that ∑iϕ(zi)≤∑iϕ(zi′) for every convex ϕ. Hint: compare top partial sums; @thm-karamata does the last step.

exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-a1.title: A1
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-a1.html:
1. State @def-unitarily-invariant-norm, saying exactly which matrices U and V range over.
  2. Explain in one sentence why a unitarily invariant norm can be computed from σ(A) alone.
  3. True or false, with a reason: A↦maxi,j|aij| is a unitarily invariant norm on M2(R).
  4. Which axiom of @def-norm is the only hard one for A↦Φ(σ(A)), and which two earlier results prove it?

exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-b1.title: B1: Which of these are unitarily invariant norms
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-b1.title_html: B1: Which of these are unitarily invariant norms
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-b1.html:
Determine which of the following are unitarily invariant norms on M2(R). Justify your answer, naming the clause that fails when one does.

  1. |||A|||=σ1(A)+σ2(A).
  2. |||A|||=|a11|+|a12|+|a21|+|a22|.
  3. |||A|||=(σ1(A)3+σ2(A)3)1/3.
  4. |||A|||=|trA|.
  5. |||A|||=max(σ1(A), 2σ2(A)).

exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-b2.title: B2: Measuring one matrix in every way
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-b2.title_html: B2: Measuring one matrix in every way
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-b2.html:
Let A=(2112),B=(2−1−12).

  1. Compute σ(A) and σ(B), and then ‖A‖2, ‖A‖F, |||A|||(1) and |||A|||(2).
  2. Compute σ(A+B) and verify σ(A+B)≺wσ(A)+σ(B) directly, saying for which k the inequality is strict.
  3. Verify @prp-ui-norm-properties (c) for A and the Frobenius norm, and check that the Frobenius norm is normalized.

exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-b3.title: B3: Moving a factor across
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-b3.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F), let |||⋅||| be a unitarily invariant norm on Mm×n(F), and let P be an orthogonal projection of Fm onto a subspace, with matrix P.

  1. Prove that ‖P‖2≤1.
  2. Deduce that |||PA|||≤|||A|||.
  3. Give an example with m=n=2 in which the inequality in (b) is strict for the Frobenius norm.

exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c1.title: C1: A gauge built from two Ky Fan gauges
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c1.title_html: C1: A gauge built from two Ky Fan gauges
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c1.html:
On Rp let Φ(x)=max(Φ1(x), 2kΦk(x)) for a fixed 2≤k≤p, with Φ1 and Φk the Ky Fan gauges of @def-ky-fan-gauge.

  1. Prove that Φ is a symmetric gauge function.
  2. Write down the unitarily invariant norm it induces on Mm×n(F), and decide whether it is normalized.
  3. For p=k=2, show that Φ(x)=max(|x|1↓, |x1|+|x2|)=|x1|+|x2|, and conclude that the norm of (b) is the trace norm in that case.

exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c2.title: C2: How much scaling submultiplicativity can stand
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c2.title_html: C2: How much scaling submultiplicativity can stand
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c2.html:
Let c>0 and consider Nc(A)=c‖A‖2 on Mn(F), n≥1.

  1. Prove that Nc is a unitarily invariant norm for every c>0, and compute its gauge.
  2. Determine exactly which c make Nc submultiplicative. Hint: test at A=B=In.
  3. Do the same for Mc(A)=c|||A|||(n), the scaled trace norm. Show that A=B=In is now the wrong test matrix, and find one that gives the sharp answer.

exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c3.title: C3: The correspondence in the smallest case
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c3.title_html: C3: The correspondence in the smallest case
exr-unitarily-invariant-norms-c3.html:
1. Describe all unitarily invariant norms on M1×n(F), the row vectors. Hint: what is p?
  2. Deduce that on M1×n(F) every unitarily invariant norm is a positive multiple of the Euclidean norm of the row.
  3. Explain why the answer to (a) does not contradict the existence of many different unitarily invariant norms on M2(F).

exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-a1.title: A1
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-a1.html:
1. Define a doubly substochastic matrix, and say which doubly substochastic matrices are doubly stochastic.
  2. State @thm-von-neumann-trace, with its hypotheses, and say what “aligned” means.
  3. Determine whether the following is true for all A,B∈Mn(C), and justify your answer: |tr(AB)|≤∑iσi(A)σi(B).
  4. Where in the proof of @thm-von-neumann-trace is the unitarity of M and N used, and what exactly is deduced from it?
  5. Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: if tr(A∗B)=∑iσi(A)σi(B) then A=B.

exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-b1.title: B1: Both sides of the inequality
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-b1.title_html: B1: Both sides of the inequality
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-b1.html: Let A=(3001),B=(0420). Compute tr(A⊤B), the singular values of both matrices, and both sides of @thm-von-neumann-trace. Then find a matrix B″ with the same singular values as B for which equality holds.

exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-b2.title: B2: The trace against the trace norm
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-b2.title_html: B2: The trace against the trace norm
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-b2.html:
Let A∈Mn(C).

  1. Prove that |trA|≤∑i=1nσi(A).
  2. Determine all A for which equality holds with A positive semidefinite.

exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-b3.title: B3: A weight matrix
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-b3.html: Let A=diag(5,1) and let B=Udiag(2,1)U∗ with U=12(1−111). Write down the matrices M and N of the proof of @thm-von-neumann-trace for this pair, the weight matrix D, and verify @eq-von-neumann-weights and the inequality numerically.

exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-c1.title: C1: The triangle inequality for the trace norm
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-c1.title_html: C1: The triangle inequality for the trace norm
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-c1.html:
Write |||A|||(p)=∑iσi(A) for the trace norm of @def-ky-fan-norm, A∈Mm×n(C).

  1. Prove that |||A|||(p)=max{|tr(A∗Q)|:Q∈Mm×n(C), ‖Q‖2≤1}.
  2. Hence deduce that |||⋅|||(p) satisfies the triangle inequality, without using @lem-singular-value-subadditive.

Hint: for (a), @cor-trace-duality with the spectral norm, read the other way round.

exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-c2.title: C2: The nearest unitary, again
exr-von-neumann-trace-inequality-c2.html:
Let A∈Mn(C) with polar decomposition A=W|A| (@thm-polar-decomposition).

  1. Prove that max{Retr(Q∗A):Q∈Mn(C) unitary}=∑iσi(A), attained at Q=W.
  2. Deduce @cor-unitary-nearest, that W minimizes ‖A−Q‖F over unitary Q.

lem-block-dilation.title: Unitary Dilation of a Contraction
lem-block-dilation.html: Let V∈Mn×m(F) be a contraction, and set D1=(Im−V∗V)1/2,D2=(In−VV∗)1/2. Then Im−V∗V⪰0 and In−VV∗⪰0, so both square roots exist, and the (n+m)×(n+m) matrix U=(VD2D1−V∗) is unitary.

lem-convex-gradient-inequality.title: A Convex Function Lies Above Its Tangent
lem-convex-gradient-inequality.title_html: A Convex Function Lies Above Its Tangent
lem-convex-gradient-inequality.html: Let I⊆R be an open interval and let f:I→R be convex and differentiable. Then f(s) ≥ f(t)+f′(t)(s−t)for all s,t∈I.

lem-divided-difference-continuous.title: Divided Differences Are Continuous
lem-divided-difference-continuous.html: Let f∈C1(I). If (sk) and (tk) are sequences in I with sk→s0∈I and tk→t0∈I, then f[sk,tk]→f[s0,t0]. In particular, for each fixed α∈I the function t↦f[α,t] is continuous on I.

lem-double-resolution-identity.title: The Two-Resolution Identity
lem-double-resolution-identity.html: Let f:I→R be differentiable and let A,B∈Mn(F) be Hermitian with spectra in I. Write the spectral resolutions A=∑iαiPi,B=∑kβkQk with αi the distinct eigenvalues of A and βk those of B (@thm-spectral-resolution). Then f(B)−f(A)=∑i,kf[αi,βk]Pi(B−A)Qk.

lem-functional-calculus-conjugation.title: Three Ways to Move the Functional Calculus
lem-functional-calculus-conjugation.title_html: Three Ways to Move the Functional Calculus
lem-functional-calculus-conjugation.html:
Let I⊆R be an interval and f:I→R.

  1. (Shift.) Let s∈R, let g(t)=f(t+s) on I−s, and let A be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I−s. Then g(A)=f(A+sI).
  2. (Unitary conjugation.) Let A be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I and let U be unitary of the same size. Then spec(U∗AU)=spec(A) and f(U∗AU)=U∗f(A)U.
  3. (Direct sums.) Let A,B be Hermitian with spectra in I. Then f(A⊕B)=f(A)⊕f(B).

lem-functional-calculus-continuous.title: Continuity of the Functional Calculus
lem-functional-calculus-continuous.html: Let J=[a,b] be a closed bounded interval, let g:J→R be continuous and let n≥1. For every ε>0 there is η>0 such that all Hermitian X,Y∈Mn(F) with spectra in J and ‖X−Y‖F<η satisfy ‖g(X)−g(Y)‖F<ε.

lem-integral-preserves-loewner.title: The Integral of a Positive Semidefinite Integrand
lem-integral-preserves-loewner.title_html: The Integral of a Positive Semidefinite Integrand
lem-integral-preserves-loewner.html: Let M:[a,b]→Mn(C) be continuous with M(s)⪰0 for every s∈[a,b]. Then ∫abM(s)ds ⪰ 0. The same conclusion holds for a convergent improper integral of a continuous integrand that is ⪰0 at every point of the interval.

lem-lie-product.title: Lie’s Product Formula
lem-lie-product.html: Let A,B∈Mn(C). Then eA+B=limk→∞(eA/keB/k)k, the limit taken entrywise, and also in any norm on Mn(C).

lem-log-derivative.title: The Derivative of the Logarithm
lem-log-derivative.html: The function log:(0,∞)→R of @lem-exp-log is differentiable with log′⁡(y)=1/y. Consequently g(t)=tlog⁡t is differentiable on (0,∞) with g′(t)=log⁡t+1 and g″(t)=1/t, and g is strictly convex there.

lem-off-diagonal-block-bound.title: The Off-Diagonal Block of a Positive Semidefinite Matrix
lem-off-diagonal-block-bound.title_html: The Off-Diagonal Block of a Positive Semidefinite Matrix
lem-off-diagonal-block-bound.html: Let k,l≥1, let P∈Mk(F), Q∈Ml(F) and X∈Mk×l(F), and suppose that M=(PXX∗Q) ⪰ 0. Then 2σj(X)≤λj(M) for every j=1,…,min(k,l).

lem-operator-monotone-composite.title: Composites of Operator Monotone Functions
lem-operator-monotone-composite.html: Let I,J be intervals, let g:I→R be operator monotone on I with g(I)⊆J, and let h:J→R be operator monotone on J. Then h∘g is operator monotone on I.

lem-operator-monotone-limit.title: Pointwise Limits Stay Operator Monotone
lem-operator-monotone-limit.html: Let fk:I→R be operator monotone on I for every k, and suppose fk(t)→f(t) for every t∈I. Then f is operator monotone on I.

lem-peierls.title: Peierls’ Inequality
lem-peierls.html: Let I⊆R be an interval, let A∈Mn(F) be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I, let f:I→R be convex, and let u∈Fn with ‖u‖=1. Then ⟨Au,u⟩∈I and f(⟨Au,u⟩) ≤ ⟨f(A)u,u⟩, with equality when u is an eigenvector of A.

lem-power-integral.title: The Integral That Represents a Power
lem-power-integral.title_html: The Integral That Represents a Power
lem-power-integral.html: Let 0<p<1. Then the improper integral Kp:=∫0∞up−11+udu converges, with 0<Kp<∞, and for every λ>0 ∫0∞sp−1λλ+sds = Kpλp.

lem-singular-value-subadditive.title: Weak Subadditivity of the Singular Values
lem-singular-value-subadditive.title_html: Weak Subadditivity of the Singular Values
lem-singular-value-subadditive.html: Let A,B∈Mm×n(F). Then σ(A+B)≺wσ(A)+σ(B), that is, ∑i=1kσi(A+B)≤∑i=1k(σi(A)+σi(B)) for every 1≤k≤p.

lem-substochastic-pairing.title: Substochastic Pairing
lem-substochastic-pairing.html: Let x1≥⋯≥xp≥0 and y1≥⋯≥yp≥0 be real numbers, and let D∈Mp(R) be doubly substochastic. Then ∑k=1p∑l=1pdklxkyl ≤ ∑k=1pxkyk.

lem-symmetric-list-top-sums.title: Top Sums of a Symmetric List
lem-symmetric-list-top-sums.title_html: Top Sums of a Symmetric List
lem-symmetric-list-top-sums.html: Let z1,…,zq be real numbers, let r≥0 be an integer, and let c∈R2q+r be the list c=(z1,…,zq, 0,…,0⏟r, −zq,…,−z1). Then for every k≤q, the largest sum of k entries of c, which is the running total ∑j≤kcj↓, equals the sum of the k largest of the numbers |z1|,…,|zq|.

lem-t-transform-step.title: One Averaging Step
lem-t-transform-step.html:
Let x,y∈Rn be decreasing, with x≺y and x≠y. Then there is a T-transform T such that y′=Ty satisfies

  1. y′ is decreasing;
  2. x≺y′;
  3. yi′=xi for strictly more indices i than yi=xi does.

lem-trace-of-a-function.title: Reading a Trace on an Orthonormal Basis
lem-trace-of-a-function.title_html: Reading a Trace on an Orthonormal Basis
lem-trace-of-a-function.html:
Let F=R or C.

  1. Let (u1,…,un) be an orthonormal basis of Fn and M∈Mn(F). Then trM=∑i=1n⟨Mui,ui⟩.
  2. Let I⊆R, let A∈Mn(F) be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I, and let g:I→R. Then g(A)u=g(λ)u for every eigenvector u of A with eigenvalue λ, and trg(A)=∑i=1ng(λi(A)).

lem-trace-of-positive-product.title: Powers of a Product of Two Positive Matrices
lem-trace-of-positive-product.title_html: Powers of a Product of Two Positive Matrices
lem-trace-of-positive-product.html: Let X,Y∈Mn(C) be positive semidefinite and let k≥1. Then tr((XY)k)=tr((X1/2YX1/2)k), and this number is real and ≥0.

lem-trace-power-inequality.title: The Trace Power Inequality
lem-trace-power-inequality.html:
Let r≥0 and m=2r.

  1. tr((A∗)mAm)≤tr((AA∗)m) for every A∈Mn(C).
  2. tr((XY)m)≤tr(XmYm) for all positive semidefinite X,Y∈Mn(C).

lem-ui-norm-of-diagonal.title: The Gauge of a Unitarily Invariant Norm
lem-ui-norm-of-diagonal.title_html: The Gauge of a Unitarily Invariant Norm
lem-ui-norm-of-diagonal.html: Let |||⋅||| be a unitarily invariant norm on Mm×n(F) and define Φ(x)=|||diagm,n(x)|||(x∈Rp). Then Φ is a symmetric gauge function on Rp, and |||A|||=Φ(σ(A))for every A∈Mm×n(F). In particular |||A||| depends on A only through σ(A).

lem-weak-majorization-dominated.title: Weak Majorization Is Domination plus Majorization
lem-weak-majorization-dominated.title_html: Weak Majorization Is Domination plus Majorization
lem-weak-majorization-dominated.html: Let x,y∈Rn. Then x≺wy if and only if there is a vector z∈Rn with x≤zentrywise,z≺y. If x has non-negative entries, then z may be taken with non-negative entries as well.

prp-gauge-monotone.title: Symmetric Gauges Are Monotone
prp-gauge-monotone.html: Let Φ be a symmetric gauge function on Rn, and let x,y∈Rn satisfy |xi|≤|yi| for every i. Then Φ(x)≤Φ(y).

prp-majorization-from-convex.title: Convex Functions Detect Majorization
prp-majorization-from-convex.html: Let x,y∈Rn. If ∑i=1nϕ(xi) ≤ ∑i=1nϕ(yi) for every convex ϕ:R→R, then x≺y.

prp-operator-convex-cone.title: Combining Operator Convex Functions
prp-operator-convex-cone.html:
Let f and g be operator convex on I.

  1. For all c≥0 and α,β∈R, the functions f+g and α+βt+cf(t) are operator convex on I.
  2. For every s∈R, the translate t↦f(t+s) is operator convex on I−s.

prp-riemann-sums-converge.title: Riemann Sums of a Continuous Matrix Function Converge
prp-riemann-sums-converge.title_html: Riemann Sums of a Continuous Matrix Function Converge
prp-riemann-sums-converge.html: Let M:[a,b]→Mp×q(C) be continuous. Then there is a matrix J∈Mp×q(C) such that S(M,Pk)→J for every sequence (Pk) of tagged partitions of [a,b] whose meshes tend to 0.

prp-t-transform-doubly-stochastic.title: T-transforms Are Doubly Stochastic
prp-t-transform-doubly-stochastic.html: Every T-transform lies in Ωn.

prp-ui-norm-properties.title: Basic Properties
prp-ui-norm-properties.html:
Let |||⋅||| be a unitarily invariant norm on Mm×n(F), with gauge Φ as in @lem-ui-norm-of-diagonal, and let A∈Mm×n(F).

  1. σ(A∗)=σ(A); consequently, if |||⋅|||′ is the unitarily invariant norm on Mn×m(F) attached to the same gauge Φ by @thm-von-neumann-correspondence, then |||A∗|||′=|||A|||. For m=n this reads |||A∗|||=|||A|||.
  2. |||XA|||≤‖X‖2|||A||| for every X∈Mm(F), and |||AY|||≤|||A|||‖Y‖2 for every Y∈Mn(F).
  3. If |||⋅||| is normalized, meaning |||e1e1∗|||=1 for the m×n matrix e1e1∗ with a single 1 in position (1,1), then ‖A‖2 ≤ |||A||| ≤ |||A|||(p).
  4. A normalized unitarily invariant norm on Mn(F) is submultiplicative: |||AB|||≤|||A||||||B|||.

prp-weak-karamata.title: Karamata for Weak Majorization
prp-weak-karamata.html: Let x,y∈Rn with x≺wy, and let ϕ:R→R be convex and increasing. Then ∑i=1nϕ(xi) ≤ ∑i=1nϕ(yi).

thm-derivative-of-a-matrix-function.title: The Derivative of a Matrix Function
thm-derivative-of-a-matrix-function.title_html: The Derivative of a Matrix Function
thm-derivative-of-a-matrix-function.html:
Let f∈C1(I), let A,H∈Mn(F) be Hermitian, and suppose there are s0>0 and a closed bounded interval J⊆I with spec(A+sH)⊆Jfor every real s with |s|<s0. Then the matrix-valued function G(s):=f(A+sH), defined for |s|<s0, is differentiable at s=0 in the sense of @def-matrix-valued-derivative, and:

  1. If A=diag(t1,…,tn), then G′(0)=Lf(t1,…,tn)∘H, the Hadamard product of @def-hadamard-product.
  2. In general, if A=UDU∗ with U unitary and D=diag(λ1,…,λn), then G′(0)=U(Lf(λ1,…,λn)∘(U∗HU))U∗.

thm-dual-gauge.title: The Dual of a Symmetric Gauge
thm-dual-gauge.title_html: The Dual of a Symmetric Gauge
thm-dual-gauge.html: Let Φ be a symmetric gauge function on Rn. Then Φ∗ is a symmetric gauge function, and Φ∗∗=Φ.

thm-gauge-monotone-under-majorization.title: Symmetric Gauges Respect Majorization
thm-gauge-monotone-under-majorization.html:
Let Φ be a symmetric gauge function on Rn.

  1. If x,y∈Rn and x≺y, then Φ(x)≤Φ(y).
  2. If x,y∈Rn have non-negative entries and x≺wy, then Φ(x)≤Φ(y).

thm-geometric-mean-properties.title: Properties of the Geometric Mean
thm-geometric-mean-properties.html:
Let A,B,A′,B′∈Mn(F) be positive definite and let S∈Mn(F) be invertible.

  1. Extremal characterization. A#B is the largest Hermitian X∈Mn(F) for which (AXXB) ⪰ 0: this holds for X=A#B, and every Hermitian X for which it holds satisfies X⪯A#B.
  2. Symmetry. A#B=B#A.
  3. Congruence. (S∗AS)#(S∗BS)=S∗(A#B)S.
  4. Monotonicity. If A⪰A′ and B⪰B′, then A#B⪰A′#B′.
  5. Arithmetic–geometric mean, and inversion. A#B⪯12(A+B), and (A#B)−1=A−1#B−1.

thm-golden-thompson.title: The Golden–Thompson Inequality
thm-golden-thompson.html: Let A,B∈Mn(C) be Hermitian. Then treA+B ≤ tr(eAeB). Both sides are real and positive, and equality holds if AB=BA.

thm-hardy-littlewood-polya.title: Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya Theorem
thm-hardy-littlewood-polya.html: Let x,y∈Rn. Then x≺y⟺x=Dy  for some D∈Ωn. Moreover, if x and y are both decreasing, D may be taken to be a product of at most n−1 T-transforms.

thm-jensen-operator.title: Hansen–Pedersen–Jensen Inequality
thm-jensen-operator.html:
Let I⊆R be an interval with 0∈I, let f:I→R be operator convex on I, let A∈Mn(F) be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I, and let V∈Mn×m(F) be a contraction. Then spec(V∗AV)⊆I, and f(V∗AV) ⪯ V∗f(A)V+f(0)(Im−V∗V). In particular:

  1. if f(0)≤0, then f(V∗AV)⪯V∗f(A)V;
  2. if V is an isometry, then f(V∗AV)⪯V∗f(A)V, with no condition on f(0).

thm-karamata.title: Karamata’s Inequality
thm-karamata.html: Let I⊆R be an interval, let ϕ:I→R be convex, and let x,y∈Rn satisfy x≺y, with every entry of y lying in I. Then every entry of x lies in I, and ∑i=1nϕ(xi) ≤ ∑i=1nϕ(yi).

thm-klein.title: Klein’s Inequality
thm-klein.html: Let I⊆R be an open interval and let f:I→R be convex and differentiable. Let A,B∈Mn(C) be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I and spec(B)⊆I. Then tr(f(A)−f(B)−(A−B)f′(B)) ≥ 0, where f(A), f(B) and f′(B) are the functional calculus of @def-function-of-normal-operator.

thm-ky-fan-dominance.title: Ky Fan Dominance Theorem
thm-ky-fan-dominance.html:
Let A,B∈Mm×n(F) with F=R or C, and let p=min(m,n). The following are equivalent.

  1. σ(A)≺wσ(B), that is, ∑i≤kσi(A)≤∑i≤kσi(B) for every k=1,…,p.
  2. |||A|||≤|||B||| for every unitarily invariant norm |||⋅||| on Mm×n(F).

thm-lidskii-convex.title: Lidskii’s Theorem, Convex Form
thm-lidskii-convex.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F) be Hermitian, F=R or C. Then for every convex ϕ:R→R, ∑i=1nϕ(λi(A)−λi(B)) ≤ ∑i=1nϕ(λi(A−B)).

thm-lidskii-ui.title: Lidskii’s Theorem, Norm Form
thm-lidskii-ui.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F) be Hermitian. Then for every unitarily invariant norm on Mn(F), 𝛌𝛌|||diag(λ(A)−λ(B))||| ≤ |||A−B|||.

thm-loewner.title: Loewner’s Theorem
thm-loewner.html:
Let f:(0,∞)→R. The following are equivalent.

  1. f is operator monotone on (0,∞).
  2. There are α∈R, β≥0 and a positive measure ν on [0,∞) with ∫(1+s2)−1dν(s)<∞ such that for every t>0 f(t)=α+βt+∫[0,∞)(s1+s2−1t+s)dν(s).
  3. f is the restriction to (0,∞) of a function analytic on C∖(−∞,0] that sends every point of the upper half-plane to a point with non-negative imaginary part.

These are the three conditions of @thm-loewner-statement.

thm-loewner-matrix-criterion.title: Loewner’s Matrix Criterion
thm-loewner-matrix-criterion.html:
Let I be an interval with more than one point, let f∈C1(I) and let n≥1. The following are equivalent.

  1. f is monotone of order n on I.
  2. Lf(t1,…,tn)⪰0 for all t1,…,tn∈I.

thm-matrix-am-gm.title: Arithmetic–Geometric Mean Inequality for Matrices
thm-matrix-am-gm.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F). Then 2σj(A∗B) ≤ λj(AA∗+BB∗)(j=1,…,n), and consequently, for every unitarily invariant norm on Mn(F), 2|||A∗B||| ≤ |||AA∗+BB∗|||.

thm-matrix-cauchy-schwarz.title: Cauchy–Schwarz for Unitarily Invariant Norms
thm-matrix-cauchy-schwarz.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F). Then for every unitarily invariant norm on Mn(F), |||A∗B|||2 ≤ |||A∗A||| |||B∗B|||.

thm-mirsky-ui.title: Mirsky’s Theorem in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm
thm-mirsky-ui.title_html: Mirsky’s Theorem in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm
thm-mirsky-ui.html: Let A,B∈Mm×n(C) and p=min(m,n). Then for every unitarily invariant norm on Mm×n(C), |||diagm,n(σ(A)−σ(B))||| ≤ |||A−B|||.

thm-operator-convex-examples.title: Four Operator Convex Functions
thm-operator-convex-examples.html:
1. Every affine function t↦α+βt is operator convex and operator concave on R.
  2. t↦t2 is operator convex on R, hence on every interval.
  3. t↦1/t is operator convex on (0,∞); equivalently, t↦−1/t is operator concave there.
  4. For every c>0, the function t↦1/(t+c) is operator convex on (0,∞), and t↦t/(t+c) is operator concave there.

thm-pick-nevanlinna.title: (A7) The Theorem of Pick and Nevanlinna
thm-pick-nevanlinna.title_html: (A7) The Theorem of Pick and Nevanlinna
thm-pick-nevanlinna.html:
Let I⊆R be an open interval and let f:I→R.

  1. Suppose that f is differentiable and that for every n≥1 and all t1,…,tn∈I the Loewner matrix Lf(t1,…,tn) of @def-loewner-matrix is positive semidefinite. Then f is the restriction to I of a function analytic on C∖(R∖I) that maps every point of the upper half-plane {z:Imz>0} to a point with non-negative imaginary part.
  2. Conversely, every function analytic on C∖(−∞,0] that maps the upper half-plane into {Imz≥0} has, on I=(0,∞), the integral representation of @thm-loewner-statement (ii): there are α∈R, β≥0 and a positive measure ν on [0,∞) with ∫(1+s2)−1dν(s)<∞ such that f(t)=α+βt+∫[0,∞)(s1+s2−1t+s)dν(s) for every t>0.
  3. A function that is operator monotone on an open interval is continuously differentiable there.

thm-symmetric-convex-is-schur-convex.title: A Symmetric Convex Function Is Schur-Convex
thm-symmetric-convex-is-schur-convex.title_html: A Symmetric Convex Function Is Schur-Convex
thm-symmetric-convex-is-schur-convex.html: Let A⊆Rn be symmetric and convex, and let G:A→R be convex and symmetric, that is, G(Pσx)=G(x) for every x∈A and every σ∈Sn. Then G is Schur-convex.

thm-trace-convex.title: The Trace of a Convex Function Is Convex
thm-trace-convex.title_html: The Trace of a Convex Function Is Convex
thm-trace-convex.html: Let I⊆R be an interval and let f:I→R be convex. Let A,B∈Mn(F) be Hermitian with spec(A)⊆I and spec(B)⊆I, and let 0≤θ≤1. Then C=θA+(1−θ)B is Hermitian with spec(C)⊆I, and trf(C) ≤ θtrf(A)+(1−θ)trf(B). In words: the Hermitian matrices with spectrum in I form a convex set, and A↦trf(A) is a convex function on it.

thm-von-neumann-correspondence.title: Unitarily Invariant Norms Are Symmetric Gauges
thm-von-neumann-correspondence.title_html: Unitarily Invariant Norms Are Symmetric Gauges
thm-von-neumann-correspondence.html: Let m,n≥1 and p=min(m,n). The assignments |||⋅||| ⟼ Φ|||⋅|||(x)=|||diagm,n(x)|||,Φ ⟼ |||A|||Φ=Φ(σ(A)) are mutually inverse bijections between the unitarily invariant norms on Mm×n(F) and the symmetric gauge functions on Rp.

thm-von-neumann-trace.title: Von Neumann’s Trace Inequality
thm-von-neumann-trace.html: Let A,B∈Mm×n(F) with F=R or C, and let p=min(m,n). Then |tr(A∗B)| ≤ ∑i=1pσi(A)σi(B). The bound is attained whenever A and B have aligned singular value decompositions, that is, whenever there are unitary U∈Mm(F) and V∈Mn(F) with A=UΣAV∗ and B=UΣBV∗, where ΣA,ΣB∈Mm×n(F) carry σi(A) and σi(B) on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
